Island1.dc.html.title: 1 · At rest: the screen sits over the camera and shows the session list

Island2.dc.html.title: 2 · The session list, swiped to change page

Island3.dc.html.title: 3 · No press: a request fills the screen, answer keys light

Island4.dc.html.title: 4a · Press allow: a short half-height confirmation, then the list

Island6.dc.html.title: 5 · Let go, read the transcript, press send

Island7.dc.html.title: 6 · No press: the agent finishes its turn

Island8.dc.html.title: Any time · Press a number: its session opens, and the wheel light comes on

Island9.dc.html.title: Hidden request · Tap the screen: the request hides, its row turns amber, the answer keys go dark

IslandLayout1.dc.html.title: Layout 1 · Touch and hold the plate: move or remove keys and the wheel

IslandLayout2.dc.html.title: Layout 2 · Add a Key lists what is not on the deck

IslandPair.dc.html.title: First run · Pair with the PC

Effort1.dc.html.title: Effort 1 · Turn the wheel: the island shows the level for the selected session

Effort2.dc.html.title: Effort 2 · Stop turning: the PC sets it once, for the next message

Effort3.dc.html.title: Effort 3 · If the PC cannot confirm the change, the island says so

Reply1.dc.html.title: Saved reply 1 · Press a saved-reply key: the island shows its text, nothing is sent yet

Reply2.dc.html.title: Saved reply 2 · Press send: it is queued for the end of the turn

t-phone.text: iPhone app: the island deck. A white outline marks the key or wheel in use
